extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors submitting papers to ACL 2025 (computational linguistics / NLP community)
extracted.subtask_description: Call-for-papers and submission policy for ACL 2025: rules, formats, topical scope, review process, and presentation/commitment requirements for authors submitting long or short papers via ARR. Includes theme-track guidance and mandatory reviewer-workload policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of substantial, original, unpublished research
rubrics_metrics.description: ACL 2025 invites the submission of long and short papers featuring substantial, original, and unpublished research in all aspects of Computational Linguistics and Natural Language Processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Papers should present new contributions; acceptable contributions broadly include traditional research results as well as negative findings, surveys, resources, position arguments, novel linguistic insights derived using existing computational techniques, and reproducibility studies (reproduce or fail to reproduce previous results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable contribution types (diversity of contributions)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to traditional research results, papers may contribute negative findings, survey an area, announce the creation of a new resource, argue a position, report novel linguistic insights derived using existing computational techniques, and reproduce, or fail to reproduce, previous results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACL 2025 has a goal of a diverse technical program; these types of contributions are explicitly welcomed and considered appropriate for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and topical fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should be on topics relevant to ACL 2025; the conference lists relevant topics (not exhaustive) including Computational Social Science, Dialogue, Discourse and Pragmatics, Efficient/Low-Resource Methods, Ethics/Bias/Fairness, Generation, Human-Centered NLP, Information Extraction, IR/Text Mining, Interpretability, Language Modeling, Linguistic theories/cognitive modeling, ML for NLP, MT, Multilinguality, Multimodality, NLP Applications, Phonology/Morphology, QA, Resources and Evaluation, Semantics, Sentiment/Stylistic/Argument Mining, Speech/TTS/SLU, Summarization, Syntax/Parsing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your paper fits within these areas or closely related NLP/CL fields, it is within scope; the list is illustrative and not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Theme Track: Generalization of NLP Models
rubrics_metrics.description: A themed track on 'Generalization of NLP Models' invites empirical/theoretical research and position/survey papers reflecting on generalization of NLP models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible topics include enhancing generalization across compositional, structural, cross-task, cross-lingual, cross-domain, and robustness dimensions; factors affecting generalization; methods for evaluating generalization; and limitations of LLMs regarding generalization. Theme submissions can be long or short and will be considered for a Thematic Paper Award and a special session.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-stage review process (Submission to ARR, Commitment to ACL 2025)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors submit articles to ACL Rolling Review (ARR) where submissions receive reviews and meta-reviews; authors then commit their reviewed articles to a publication venue (e.g., ACL 2025) where Senior Area Chairs and Program Chairs make acceptance decisions based on ARR reviews and meta-reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must follow this two-step process to commit; after a paper has been fully reviewed, authors may either commit to a conference or revise and resubmit for another ARR round. ARR reviews and meta-reviews are used by ACL decision-makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARR submission required for commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers may be submitted to the ARR 2025 February cycle; only papers that have received reviews and a meta-review from ARR may be committed to ACL 2025 via the conference commitment site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must submit to ARR (in the specified cycle or an earlier ARR cycle) to obtain the reviews/meta-review necessary for commitment to ACL 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind reviewing / anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewing process will continue to be double-blind: Reviewers will not see authors, nor will authors see reviewers, and reviews on ARR will not be made publicly visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are given the option through ARR to make their anonymized submitted articles publicly visible; follow ARR's 'Instructions for Two-Way Anonymized Review' (referenced in ARR requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory reviewing workload declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: During the ARR submission process, authors will be required to specify which co-authors are committing to cover reviewing in this reviewing cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an ARR-wide policy to strengthen commitment to reviewing; consult the ARR policy regarding reviewing workload for details and clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper length and formats (long and short papers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Long Papers: 8 pages. Short Papers: 4 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final versions of accepted papers will be given one additional page of content (up to 9 pages for long papers, up to 5 pages for short papers) to address reviewers’ comments. Follow ARR submission templates and page-count rules precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow ARR submission requirements and policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Both long and short paper submissions should follow all of the ARR submission requirements, including: Instructions for Two-Way Anonymized Review; Authorship; Citation and Comparison; Multiple Submission Policy; Resubmission Policy; and Withdrawal Policy; Ethics Policy including the responsible NLP research checklist; and Limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These referenced policies contain substantive requirements (e.g., how to anonymize, how to declare authorship, how to cite and compare prior work, what constitutes multiple submission/resubmission, withdrawal procedures, ethics checklist, and limits statements). Authors must consult and comply with each linked ARR/ACL policy item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics policy and responsible NLP research checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must comply with the Ethics Policy, including completion of the responsible NLP research checklist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure ethical considerations, harms, dataset/privacy issues, and other responsible-research elements are disclosed as required by the checklist and policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations statement requirement (referenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are expected to follow the ARR policy on Limitations (the CFP lists 'Limitations' among ARR requirements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear limitations of the work per ACL/ARR guidance (e.g., discuss boundaries of claims, dataset/method limitations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional supplementary materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit optional supplementary materials with their submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary materials are optional and should follow ARR/ACL rules regarding what is permitted and how they will be used in review.

rubrics_metrics.name: No anonymity period requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the ACL and ARR policies, there is no anonymity period requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may, at submission time via ARR, choose to make their anonymized submitted articles publicly visible; there is not a required period during which papers must remain anonymous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting preferred venue at ARR submission is non-binding
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of submission to ARR, authors will be asked to select a preferred venue (e.g., ACL 2025); this is used only to calculate acceptance rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors who selected ACL 2025 as preferred may still choose not to commit after receiving reviews; authors who selected a different preferred venue may still commit to ACL 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and registration requirement for proceedings inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: All accepted papers must be presented at the conference to appear in the proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The conference will include in-person and virtual presentation options. Papers without at least one presenting author registered by the early registration deadline may be subject to desk rejection. Long and short papers may be presented orally or as posters as determined by the program committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation format and proceedings notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Long and short papers will be presented orally or as posters as determined by the program committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short papers will be distinguished from long papers in the proceedings, but there will be no distinction in the proceedings between papers presented orally and papers presented as posters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic consideration for Findings if not selected for main conference
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers submitted to ACL 2025, but not selected for the main conference, will also automatically be considered for publication in the Findings of the Association of Computational Linguistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors need not separately submit to Findings in this case; automatic consideration is part of the pipeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Important deadlines and timeline constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Key dates: Submission deadline (Feb 15, 2025); ARR reviews & meta-reviews available (Apr 15, 2025); Commitment deadline for ACL 2025 (Apr 20, 2025); Notification of acceptance (May 15, 2025); Withdrawal and camera-ready deadline (May 30, 2025); Conference dates (July 27–Aug 1, 2025). All deadlines are at 11:59PM UTC-12:00 (anywhere on Earth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must meet these dates; commitment and registration deadlines are particularly consequential for acceptance and proceedings inclusion. Consult the CFP for event-specific dates (tutorials, main conference, workshops).
